name: B-Frame Consistency Analysis
description: Analyzes bidirectional frame consistency — deepfake injection disrupts natural B-frame interpolation patterns.
mechanism:
This method analyzes B-frame prediction patterns in video compression for forensic authentication following Sullivan et al. (2012):

1. **GOPStructure분석**: The Group of Pictures (GOP) structure is parsed to identify I-frames (intra-coded), P-frames (predictive), and B-frames (bidirectional predictive). The expected B-frame pattern depends on codec configuration and is consistent in unmanipulated video.

2. **Bi-DirectionalPredictionResidual**: B-frames use both forward and backward temporal prediction. The prediction residuals are analyzed — in authentic video, B-frame residuals are typically smaller than P-frame residuals due to the advantage of bidirectional prediction. Manipulated regions produce anomalous residual patterns where inserted content disrupts the predicted motion trajectory.

3. **동작벡터일관성**: B-frame motion vectors point both forward and backward in time. The method checks whether forward and backward motion vectors are physically consistent — they should describe complementary views of the same motion. Deepfake insertion creates motion vector inconsistencies where forward and backward predictions disagree abnormally.

4. **QuantizationParameter추적**: Per Stamm et al. (2012), the quantization parameters (QP) assigned to B-frames follow predictable patterns relative to reference frames. Double-encoding artifacts from video manipulation alter these QP patterns, creating detectable statistical anomalies in the B-frame quantization structure.

5. **시간적DependencyGraph검증**: The reference frame dependencies of B-frames are verified for consistency. Inserted or replaced frames disrupt the expected temporal dependency chain, producing frames that reference incorrect temporal contexts — detectable through prediction error analysis.
